limited_overlap.description: 963 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 73,860 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
184 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10028 of 12000 applicants answered (83.6%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.29 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0002, causal_forest=-0.0007.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -8.3; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -1.31. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 16384 (90% 3230 to 29538).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 2985 (90% 2128 to 3842); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -4902, without months_unemployed = 3861, without education = 3753; full model = 4087.
Run time 20 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10028.
